# Home/runtime declaration fixture

This overlay reuses the invented five-seat Harbor/Orchard configuration, using its relative resource paths and the current shared Structure, Access, Agents and Host bodies. It adds Homes and Runtime, with no Identity grant. No real account, credential or agent home is referenced.

```sh
bash tests/fixtures/home-runtime-workplace/prepare.sh /absolute/new/config
```

The destination must be new and its parent must exist. The script copies source only: no PLAN, BUILD, runtime file, secret value or generated home. It does not call the reader/frame or start a server. The materialized workplace.json lists the six selected bodies. The default socket is not selected.

Navigator has a kept home, two extra variables (cache and the home itself via dot), and the root-relative seed path tools/seed-home. Gardener has a scratch home with a cache variable. The existing two none selections stay none. Four RUNTIME files each add one distinct environment name at workplace, office, room and seat scope. Watch's ordinary environment supplies only WORKPLACE_ROLE. No supplied runtime value is authored.

This is the second source edition, following definition5.49. An ordinary environment assignment to a name supplied by that seat's home or expected runtime values refuses plan and build; it does not test precedence between two accepted values. Private variants restore NAV_HOME and NAV_CACHE separately, add an assignment to Watch's required RUN_WORKPLACE, and check an accepted assignment to RUN_SEAT, which Pilot expects but Watch does not. The first edition's two colliding rows and original expectations remain in commit5b1a995 and the private measurement history.

For a later isolated runtime rehearsal, first copy the existing reader-workplace/root support tree under the new root, then add this fixture's root/tools/seed-home. The seed merely writes its declared-directory arguments, in order, to its own provided home. It is a support executable outside the configuration input closure and must exist at the root-relative path; this source stop never invokes it through the frame. A private dummy-home safety probe checks its file replacement without building or starting a workplace. Ordinary tool directories and data must be supplied before build/up, not replaced by empty claims of functioning tools.

The source stop validates declaration formation and the emitted recorded terms. Independent expected events, per-seat decisions, frame refusals and later runtime cases are frozen privately before native measurement. Their outcomes are not disclosed in this repository during comparison. The whole runtime file must be valid before any seat expecting a value starts. Runtime-file representation belongs to the frame contract; no guessed secret-bearing file format is published here.

NATIVE-RECEIPT-v1.json is historical evidence for the first edition at5b1a995, with its exact original input hashes. It does not validate the second edition. A new native receipt must identify the second edition's inputs and freeze separately.

No statement here claims that native parsing enforces frame conflicts, home isolation, seeding, runtime-value secrecy or persistence. See docs/homes-runtime.md for the boundary. Class restrictions are ordinary Typify declarations, not a specialized home or environment implementation in the reader.
